title: Add A/B testing dashboards + guardrail alert templates (latency/error/exposure)
author: Allison Grant
release_notes: Adds initial Grafana dashboards + alert rule templates for route-level A/B experiments (variant comparisons, exposure volume, guardrail regressions).
body:
## Summary
This PR adds the initial Grafana dashboards and alert rule templates for Route-level A/B experiments.

Dashboards focus on:
- Variant comparisons for latency (p50/p95/p99) + TTFT
- Error/timeout/429 rates by variant
- Exposure volume + configured split sanity checks
- Cost attribution (tokens + GPU cost where available) by variant
- Guardrail-focused panels designed to pair with the auto-rollback evaluator

Alerts focus on:
- Latency regression vs control (p95 and p99)
- Error rate regression vs control (5xx + timeouts)
- 429 spike (capacity pressure) by region
- Exposure volume anomalies (sudden drop to near-zero; split drift)

These are templates intended for import into the hosted control-plane Grafana as well as Dedicated stacks. Private/on-prem can consume the same dashboards assuming the metrics pipeline exports the required series.

## Context / Motivation
As we enable the Console-first route A/B framework, we need standard dashboards/alerts that work across Hosted + Dedicated and avoid high-cardinality footguns.

This PR aligns with:
- Experiment metrics schema v1 (dimensions: experiment_id, variant, route_id; optional: project_id, region)
- Cardinality guardrails: no user_id/session_id, avoid raw api_key_id, etc.
- Guardrail policy work owned by SRE (alert thresholds are conservative defaults)

## What’s included
### Dashboards
1) **A/B Experiment Overview (v1)**
- Top-line status: exposures/min, requests/min, % split by variant
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end + TTFT (streaming)
- Errors: 5xx rate, timeouts, 429 rate
- Cost: tokens/request, $/1K tokens (if exported), GPU ms/request (Dedicated)
- Drilldowns: filter by experiment_id, route_id, region, variant

2) **A/B Experiment Variant Comparison (v1)**
- Side-by-side panels for A vs B (control vs treatment)
- Delta panels: p95 latency delta, error rate delta
- “Read me first” panel explaining that deltas are observational and subject to sample size + time window selection

3) **A/B Experiment Exposure Debug (v1)**
- Exposure events vs request count (to catch missing instrumentation)
- Split drift chart (configured % vs observed %) and a note about hashing stickiness
- Retry/stream reconnect counter panels (helps detect assignment instability)

### Alerts (Prometheus/Mimir-style rules)
- `ABExperimentLatencyRegressionP95` and `ABExperimentLatencyRegressionP99`
- `ABExperimentErrorRateRegression`
- `ABExperiment429Spike`
- `ABExperimentExposureDrop`
- `ABExperimentSplitDrift`

Alerts are scoped to `experiment_id` and `region` by default, and explicitly avoid dimensions known to explode cardinality.

## Implementation notes
- Introduces a common dashboard variable set:
  - `$experiment_id` (required)
  - `$route_id` (optional)
  - `$region` (optional)
  - `$variant` (optional)
- All PromQL queries use the allowlisted label set only. Where cost metrics are absent, panels render as “No data” (expected in some stacks until cost attribution rollout is complete).
- Adds a small `README.md` to document required series names + label expectations.

## Screenshots
(omitted here; see attached images in the PR UI)

## Testing
- Imported dashboards into staging Grafana (hosted) and validated queries against dogfood experiment `exp_9b2f...`.
- Verified alert rules load successfully in `mimirtool rules lint`.
- Confirmed no queries use forbidden labels (api_key_id/user_id).

## Rollout
- Dashboards: can be merged immediately; Console UI links will follow once the experiment results page is enabled.
- Alerts: defaults are OFF by policy; SRE will enable per-environment alongside guardrail evaluator rollout.

## Follow-ups
- Add quality/evals panels once eval summary artifacts are ingested into metrics/logs (Phase 2).
- Add “control-plane assignment failures” panel when the assignment service exports error counters.

notable_snippets:
Alert rule excerpt (alerts/ab-testing/ab-experiment-guardrails-v1.yaml):
- alert: ABExperimentLatencyRegressionP95
  expr: |
    (
      histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, experiment_id, variant, region) (rate(redwood_inference_request_latency_seconds_bucket{experiment_id!="",variant!=""}[5m])))
    )
    /
    (
      histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, experiment_id, region) (rate(redwood_inference_request_latency_seconds_bucket{experiment_id!="",variant="control"}[5m])))
    )
    > 1.15
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "A/B experiment p95 latency regression >15%"
    runbook: "https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SRE/ab-testing-emergency-disable-and-rollback"

Dashboard variable note (dashboards/ab-testing/README.md):
- Required labels: experiment_id, variant
- Optional labels: route_id, region, project_id
- Forbidden labels: user_id, session_id, raw_api_key, request_id
- Recommended time range: >= 30m for guardrail interpretation
review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher: The split drift alert worries me a bit—can we make sure it’s not noisy for low traffic experiments? Also want the runbook link in every alert.

Allison Grant (author): Good call. Updated SplitDrift to require >= 200 exposures in the window and added runbook annotations across the group.

Logan Wright: Queries look mostly fine. Please avoid `project_id` in alert labels—cardinality can get high for large customers. Dashboard filters are fine.

Allison Grant: Removed project_id from alert grouping/labels; kept it as an optional dashboard variable only.

Nadia Rahman: For the cost panels, can we fall back cleanly when the metering series isn’t present? Right now it shows a query error.

Allison Grant: Fixed by using `or vector(0)` and an explicit panel description that cost panels may be empty until metering rollout. Also added a transformation to hide zeros when no data.

Aisha Bello: +1. Can we add an exposure-vs-requests panel? We saw missing exposure events during dogfood.

Allison Grant: Added to Exposure Debug dashboard and included a note on typical causes (gateway sampling disabled / missing experiment_id tag).

Sean Gallagher: Approving once CI is green.
